T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others
on 17 October, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Justice Dr. V.R.K.Krupa Sagar
 Macma No.247 of 2023
Judgment:

entities.text: T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1. A father who lost his son in an automobile accident also lost his claim for compensation before the claims tribunal is flummoxed and preferred this appeal before this court under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 impugning the order dated 03.02.2016 of learned Chirman, Motor Vehicles Claims tribunal - Cum - Additional District Judge, Narsapur of West Godavari District in M.V.O.P.No.63 of 2012.
2.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Claims tribunal - Cum - Additional District Judge, Narsapur of West Godavari District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1st respondent was the driver.
2nd respondent was the owner.
3rd respondent was the insurer of the offending lorry.
3. Sri A.Veeraswamy, learned counsel for appellant and Smt. A.Jayanti, learned counsel for 3rd respondent/Insurance company submitted arguments.
4. The present appellant Sri T.Sanjeeva Rao had two sons.
The name of his younger son is T.Nagaraju.

On 12.05.2011, this T. Nagaraju was travelling in an auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 37 A 0754 going to Palakol Village and about 8.45 p.m., in the night near St.Mary's Convent, a lorry bearing No.AP 5T 1656 came in the opposite direction and came to the wrong side of the Dr. VRKS,
J road and by the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the said lorry a collision took place as the lorry dashed against auto rickshaw and as a result Sri T.Nagaraju fell down from the auto rickshaw and the tyres of the lorry ran over his body causing serious injuries.
The injured was taken to Government General Hospital, Palakol and within few hours he died out of those injuries.

The grief stricken father Sri T.Sanjeeva Rao moved his application under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 seeking compensation of Rs.5,10,000/-.
The driver, owner, insurers were shown as respondents in M.V.O.P.No.63 of 2012.
Police registered FIR and investigated into the case and filed a charge sheet before the learned Magistrate attributing rash or negligent driving as the cause of death of Mr.T.Nagaraju.
5. Before the claims tribunal, the driver and owner of the offending vehicle did not put up any contest.

The insurance company protested the claim contending that non-impleadment of driver,
owner and insurer of auto rickshaw bearing registration No. AP 37 A 0754 which was also involved in the accident was fatal to the case.
The compensation claimed is excessive.
That the claimant is not entitled to any compensation.
That the claim made is frivolous and vexatious.
Dr. VRKS, J 6.

On the rival pleadings, the claims tribunal settled the following issues for trial:
T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173490063/
1 Issues: -
1.

entities.text: T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent manner of driving of driver of vehicle lorry bearing No.AP 5 T 1656 by 1st respondent?
2. Whether there was contributory negligence of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent?

4. To what relief?
The claimant/father of the deceased/appellant herein testified as PW.1 and he also got examined an eyewitness to the accident as PW.2.
Copies of FIR, Post mortem certificate, Motor vehicles Inspector's report, charge sheet were all exhibited and they became Ex.A1 to A5.
Insurance company did not produce any oral evidence and it produced Ex.B1 which is a copy of the insurance policy.

Though the claim was under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the learned claims tribunal after extensive discussion of evidence finally concluded that lorry bearing No.AP 5T 1656 was driven rashly or negligently by its Dr. VRKS, J driver and that was the cause of the accident and that there was no fault on part of deceased or the driver of the auto rickshaw in which the deceased was travelling at the material point of time.
Based on evidence on record, it concluded that Sri T.Nagaraju died because of injuries sustained in this motor vehicle accident.
It gave categorical finding that the age of the deceased was found 23 years by the time of accident.
Thereafter the learned claims tribunal considered the evidence of the claimant/PW.1/appellant herein.
The evidence was that the claimant has been an agricultural coolie getting Rs.200 per day and is able to live on his own.
With such finding claims tribunal concluded that the claimant being father of the deceased is not entitled to any compensation since father is not a dependent on his son.
With that finding it dismissed the claim in toto.
7. As against that the father is in appeal here contending that judgment of the claims tribunal is contrary to all the legal principles.
That the father is a dependent on the deceased son.
The deceased son was hale and healthy and was aged 23 years and was earning Rs.3,300/- per month by doing milk vending business.
Failure of tribunal is very apparent as it failed even to consider to grant any compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses, loss of love and affection.

During arguments,
Dr. VRKS, J the learned counsel for appellant argued that the appellant who is father of the deceased is dependent on his son and by the time of the claim itself this father was aged 50 years.
It cannot be said that in his advanced age he could live without any support of his son who died at his young age.
It is on these submissions, the appellant challenges the impugned award of the claims tribunal.
In support of his contentions learned counsel for appellant cited Sukhdev Prasad V. Sunil Kumar1and Indrawathi V. Ranbir Singh2.
In the above referred judgments, a learned Judge of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court considered the precedent and held that parents are dependents of deceased children in motor vehicles accident claims.

8. As against that Smt.A.Jayanthi learned counsel for respondent No.3 /the oriental insurance company argued that sympathies have no place in application of principles of law and the law as is T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173490063/

Sidarapu Gongaiah3.

entities.text: New India 2021 SCC Online Delhi 2469 2021 SCC Online Delhi 114 Dr. VRKS,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: J Assurance Company Ltd V. Sidarapu Gongaiah3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That was a case where claimant Nos.2 and 4 were the adult sons of the deceased and claimant No.3 was a married daughter of the deceased.
On evidence it was found that they were not the dependents on the deceased.

It was in those circumstances a learned Judge of this court declined to grant any compensation towards loss of dependency but granted compensation towards loss of estate, loss of love and affection, funereal expenses and transport charges.

9. Therefore, the point that falls for consideration in this appeal is:
"Whether a father/appellant is entitled for any compensation for the death of his son and whether the impugned award is incorrect at law?"

POINT: -
This appeal has been argued on the following undisputed facts.

Deceased was a bachelor aged 23 years, engaged in milk vending business earning about Rs.3,300/-
per month.
He died in an auto mobile accident.
He had a father and elder brother.
2012 Lawsuit (AP) 760 Dr. VRKS, J
His elder brother did not claim any compensation.
His father alone claimed compensation.
It is that father who is in appeal here.
The father by his own evidence as PW.1 said that he himself has been earning Rs.200/- per day and he has been an agricultural coolie.
In his cross-examination, he admitted that he is capable of maintaining himself with his own income.
Thus, the evidence on record indicated independent income for the father.
When such father lost his younger son whether any compensation can be granted or not is the point at controversy.
10. It naturally occurs to mind that young children are to be maintained by their parents while the old parents are to be maintained by their children.
At a point of time even if parents are not dependent on their children, time would take a toll and the parents grow older and they become dependents on their children.

Claim for maintenance under Section 125 Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 and principles contained in Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 and Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 do indicate obligation of children to maintain their parents.

entities.text: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, in a claim for compensation in an automobile accident one of the major heads of compensation is loss of dependency.
This concept is based on assessment of a particular fact.
The Dr. VRKS, J tribunal has to find out whether the deceased performed an act for the benefit of the survivor or not.
In other words, whether the income deceased used to earn is one on which the survivor is dependent on.

If the survivor is dependent on that income of the deceased then the tribunal is under a legal obligation to consider the relevant parameters and quantify an amount of compensation which could be awarded towards loss of dependency.
It has to be borne in mind, the claim of a father for compensation under the head - loss of dependency - is dependent on the fact whether he is dependent on the earnings of his son or not.
If the father is found not dependent on his son, then the father is not entitled to reap a claim under the head loss of dependency.

In National T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173490063/
3

entities.text: National T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance Company Ltd V. Pranay Sethi4 a Constitution Bench of Five Judges of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, after considering all the principles and the precedent, gave imprimatur to the principle at paragraph No.37 of the judgment.

entities.text: Insurance Company Ltd V. Pranay Sethi4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Their Lordships held that subject to the evidence to the contrary, the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependent.
If the deceased is survived by parents and siblings, only the mother would be considered to be a dependent.
Thus, every (2017) 16 SCC 680 Dr. VRKS, J case has to be considered in accordance with the evidence available on record.
In the case at hand, the undisputed evidence indicated financial non-dependency of the father/appellant.
Thus, the death of his earning son could not give a right to claim compensation under the head - loss of dependency for the father/appellant.
In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the two rulings of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi cited for the appellant do not yield any assistance.

In these circumstances, the refusal of the claims tribunal in not granting any compensation to the father/appellant towards loss of dependency is in accordance with law and does not require any interference.
11. However, in the case at hand, the claims tribunal failed to grant any compensation to the claimant.
That cannot be countenanced.
There are conventional heads where under claimants are entitled to have compensation.
For instance, a father losing his son must be granted filial consortium.
The father must have spent money for funeral of his son and therefore he must be paid some amount of compensation towards funeral expenses.

The help and other assistance normally rendered by a son to the father and the family are no more available because of the death of the son and such loss Dr. VRKS, J has to be compensated under the head - loss of estate.

On these aspects,
the earlier referred Pranay Sethi's case itself had standardized the amounts of compensation to be granted as mentioned below:
1. Towards loss of Consortium Rs.40,000/-
2. Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

3 . Towards funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
12.
All the above heads of compensation must be granted but the claims tribunal was hasty in not granting even the above referred amounts.
Therefore, to that extent, the award of the claims tribunal cannot be supported.
The appellant/father must have spent money towards transportation charges and the same is fixed at Rs.10,000/-.
Thus, a total compensation of Rs.80,000/- can be granted to the appellant.
Over this amount he is entitled for 7.5% interest from the date of petition till the date of this order.
Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay this.
Respondent No.3/Insurance Company shall deposit these amounts before the claims tribunal within 30 days from the date of this order.
Appellant is entitled for proportionate costs all throughout.
Dr. VRKS, J 13.
In the result, this appeal is allowed in part in the following terms:
T.Sanjeeva Rao, W.G.Dist vs A.Chantiah, W.G.Dist And 2 Others on 17 October, 2023
